address: Goodwood Park Hotel, 22 Scotts Road, Singapore
w: Goodwood Park's Sichuan-Cantonese dining room since 1982 — one of Singapore's most respected Chinese restaurants (Frommer's), famous for its wood-fired Beijing duck carved at the table and served in two courses; refurbished in 2020 with Ernesto Bedmar interiors. Reviewed by critic Andy Hayler.

dish: Mao Shan Wang durian mousse cake and durian crêpes
n: Goodwood Park Hotel Coffee Lounge (durian desserts)
address: Goodwood Park Hotel, 22 Scotts Road, Singapore
w: The hotel coffee lounge behind Singapore's best-known durian desserts: the Mao Shan Wang mousse cake, crêpes and Swiss rolls sold year-round and a seasonal all-you-can-eat durian dessert buffet each mid-year — covered annually by Eatbook and Time Out, and a long-running SGFoodOnFoot favourite.

dish: Hokkien popiah — juicy braised turnip, egg, prawn and crispy fish bits, finished with lard
address: #01-16 Newton Food Centre, 500 Clemenceau Avenue North, Singapore 229495 (Makansutra prints #01-12 — unit to confirm)
w: A Hokkien popiah stall founded in 1930 and at Newton since 1977: fresh-wrapped rolls packed with juicy braised turnip, beansprouts, egg, prawn and crispy fish bits — one of the few non-seafood stalls Makansutra, Women's Weekly and Seth Lui all pick at Newton.

dish: French-Japanese plated desserts and entremets; Chef's Table dessert omakase
w: Pastry chef Makoto Arami (ex-executive pastry chef of Michelin-starred Béni and Marina Bay Sands) turned a 2021 online cult following into a black-and-white colonial bungalow off Scotts Road: a café of intricate Japanese-produce, French-technique pastries plus an eight-seat dessert-omakase room — covered by Tatler, The Peak, ladyironchef and SGFoodOnFoot.

dish: Cantonese private-dining course menu — abalone, roast pork, wagyu
w: An eight-seat Cantonese private-dining room near Newton serving course menus built on abalone, pork and wagyu — listed in Eatbook's Newton guide and reviewed by SGFoodOnFoot (2024).

dish: Old-school Cantonese classics and dim sum
address: Shangri-La Singapore, Orange Grove Road, Singapore 258350
w: Singapore's oldest hotel-run Chinese restaurant, opened with the Shangri-La in 1971 in Newton's Orange Grove: a Chinese-garden dining room serving an extensive menu of old-time Cantonese classics hard to find elsewhere — featured by the MICHELIN Guide among its business-lunch picks; the dim sum menu is the affordable way in (Ordinary Patrons, 2024).

dish: Teochew steamed pomfret; Puning steamed kampong chicken with fermented beans
address: Chui Huay Lim Club, Keng Lee Road, Newton, Singapore (unit + postal to confirm at geocode)
w: Often ranked among Singapore's top Teochew restaurants, on the ground floor of the 180-year-old Chui Huay Lim Club where prominent Teochew families have long gathered: traditional Singapore-Teochew cooking — steamed pomfret, Puning kampong chicken with fermented beans, Teochew set menus. Covered by Time Out, live2makan and SGFoodOnFoot; still reviewed in June 2026.

dish: Cod or haddock & chips (UK-imported fish, 1950s family batter recipe); fried Mars bar
n: Smiths Authentic British Fish and Chips (Balmoral Plaza)
address: Balmoral Plaza, 271 Bukit Timah Road #01-02, Singapore
w: Since 2006, two British founders have run what they call Singapore's only true British chippy: UK-imported cod and haddock in the founder's grandfather's 1950s batter, plus cottage pie and the deep-fried Mars bar — reviewed by Eatbook, Seth Lui, City Nomads and Time Out.

dish: Snow-aged Niigata wagyu and Angus steaks from the grill
address: Shangri-La Singapore, Orange Grove Road, Singapore 258350
w: The Shangri-La's lobby-level grill specialising in carefully selected grilled meats and line-caught seafood — grass- and grain-fed Australian and Irish Angus and wagyu, and exclusive snow-aged full-blood wagyu from Niigata — reviewed by The Peak, Honeycombers and SGFoodOnFoot.

dish: International buffet — sushi & sashimi, seafood on ice, dim sum, made-to-order roti prata, noodle bar
address: Shangri-La Singapore, 22 Orange Grove Road, Singapore 258350
w: The Shangri-La's garden-and-pool-view buffet since 2005 — sixteen live stations from sushi, sashimi and seafood on ice to dim sum, Indian curries, made-to-order roti prata, a noodle bar and Singaporean hawker staples; Miss Tam Chiak calls it the buffet to be at, and it's reviewed by Seth Lui and Time Out.

dish: BBQ sambal stingray with chinchalok and lime; chilli-crab-sauce lala
address: #01-53 Newton Food Centre, 500 Clemenceau Avenue North, Singapore 229495
w: A halal-certified Newton BBQ-seafood stall whose sambal stingray — fleshy fish under heaps of smoky, fiery hei bee sambal, with chinchalok and lime on the side — Miss Tam Chiak rates among the best in the centre; also does lala in thick chilli-crab sauce. Named in Eatbook's Newton guide.

dish: English afternoon tea buffet — scones with clotted cream, finger sandwiches, savouries, pastries
address: Goodwood Park Hotel, 22 Scotts Road, Singapore 228221
w: Goodwood Park's poolside café, a byword for elegant teatime since 1968: a daily English afternoon tea buffet of dainty sandwiches, savouries, pastries, a chocolate fountain and traditional scones — reviewed by Miss Tam Chiak, Seth Lui, Little Day Out and SGFoodOnFoot (2022).

address: Shangri-La Singapore, 22 Orange Grove Road, Singapore 258350
w: A garden-set Italian at the Shangri-La, now cooking the Southern Italian dishes of chef de cuisine Simone Loisi's home region of Puglia — handmade pastas and fresh seafood; reviewed by TheSmartLocal and ladyironchef, and revisited by SGFoodOnFoot in July 2025.
